newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk opposition leader's house in bug search.
newsitem.headline: Turk opposition leader's house in bug search.

text.p: Turkish opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz's house is to be searched for listening devices after electronic signals were detected emanating from behind wall panels, Anatolian news agency said on Thursday.
The house, in a plush district of Ankara, will be searched on Friday, the state-run agency said. It said a notary would be present but did not say who would carry out the search.
Anatolian said short-wave signals that could be picked up from nearby buildings or cars had been detected in Yilmaz's office and a room used for meetings, both on the third floor of the house.
Motherland Party (ANAP) leader Yilmaz, a former prime minister, has been leading calls for an investigation of a scandal linking a senior police official, a fugitive gangster and a Kurdish MP.
Yilmaz said this week he had received unspecified threats in relation to the scandal. He has said in the past the telephone in his house was being tapped.

"He has complained to us before that his house and even his mobile phone were being listened to. Because of that, he began using a mobile phone registered to someone else," ANAP deputy Hayrettin Uzun told Reuters.
